title: Outdoor Cultivation — Quantification Layer
purpose: Turn each outdoor subtopic into a repeatable field-observation workflow so learners can measure site conditions, preserve context, compare observations and make bounded decisions instead of relying on generic rules.

measurementPrinciples.title: Measure before changing
measurementPrinciples.detail: Capture the condition that exists before an intervention. Without a baseline, improvement or deterioration cannot be separated from normal variation.

measurementPrinciples.title: Repeat at comparable times and places
measurementPrinciples.detail: Outdoor conditions change by hour, weather and canopy position. Repeat measurements at the same point, depth and approximate time when comparing days.

measurementPrinciples.title: Separate measured, estimated and unknown
measurementPrinciples.detail: Label direct measurements, model or app estimates, and unknowns separately so confidence is visible instead of implied.

measurementPrinciples.title: Use trends, not isolated numbers
measurementPrinciples.detail: One reading can be useful, but repeated observations tied to weather and plant response usually support stronger conclusions.

calculations.name: Direct-sun duration
calculations.formula: direct sun end time − direct sun start time
calculations.use: Compare candidate sites and track seasonal changes in obstruction and sun angle.
calculations.boundary: Hours of direct sun do not equal DLI because light intensity changes through the day.

calculations.name: Rain depth to area volume
calculations.formula: 1 mm rain on 1 m² = 1 L water
calculations.use: Translate rainfall depth into the maximum water arriving at a horizontal area before interception, runoff and drainage losses.
calculations.boundary: It does not prove that the same volume entered the active root zone.

calculations.name: Water-source flow
calculations.formula: flow rate = collected volume ÷ collection time
calculations.use: Compare source flow at the beginning and far end of the delivery system using the same container and test duration.
calculations.boundary: Flow alone does not describe pressure, emitter uniformity or infiltration.

calculations.name: Observed wind-source overlap
calculations.formula: overlap % = observations with wind arriving from the source sector ÷ total wind observations × 100
calculations.use: Describe how often a known neighboring pollen/dust source was upwind during the observation window.
calculations.boundary: This is a screening metric, not a pollen exposure probability.

sections.learnerQuestion: Is this site suitable across the actual season, or does it only look suitable during one visit?

sourceContext.citation: Nimmala M, Ross SD, Foroutan H. Cannabis pollen dispersal across the United States. Scientific Reports. 2024;14:20605. doi:10.1038/s41598-024-70633-x.
sourceContext.supports: Cannabis pollen transport varies with meteorology, time of day, season and distance, so neighboring-source risk should be recorded as a changing landscape variable rather than reduced to one universal radius.

sourceContext.citation: Oregon State University Extension. Optimum irrigation for CBD-type hemp plants in the field. EM 9571.
sourceContext.supports: Field water response depends on cultivar type, density, irrigation method and climate, supporting site-specific water-access and delivery measurements instead of one universal irrigation amount.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Map sun over the season, not one afternoon
subtopics.goal: Quantify how much unobstructed light opportunity the plant position actually receives as sun angle, day length and obstacles change.

measure.method: From the intended canopy position, record when direct sunlight first reaches the site and when it becomes blocked. Note every major shade interruption rather than counting only sunrise-to-sunset.
measure.frequency: Repeat on representative early-, mid- and late-season dates; repeat after major vegetation or structure changes.

measure.method: Record the direction of trees, walls, fences and terrain that create shade. Photograph from the same marked position so seasonal changes can be compared.
measure.frequency: Baseline before planting and whenever the obstruction changes.

measure.method: If a calibrated PAR sensor or logger is available, measure at canopy height over the day. Keep sensor position and logging interval consistent.
measure.frequency: Use representative clear and cloudy days if comparing sites.

record: site ID and exact measurement point
sensor model and height when PAR/DLI is measured
compare: candidate sites on comparable weather days
measured PAR/DLI against direct-sun duration without assuming the two are interchangeable
interpret: A site can lose useful late-season exposure even if it was open earlier in the year.
Long direct-sun duration does not guarantee the same DLI under clouds, haze or partial obstruction.
Late-day shade may also lengthen post-rain or dew drying, so light and disease-weather context should be considered together.
subtopics.decisionRule: Choose the site from whole-season exposure and drying opportunity. Do not approve or reject a site from one noon observation or one universal 'minimum sun hours' number.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: High confidence requires repeated site-specific observations or calibrated measurements; app-only sun-path estimates should be labeled estimated until field-verified.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Drainage and topography shape the root environment
subtopics.goal: Quantify where water enters, ponds, infiltrates and leaves the site after real rain or irrigation.

measure.method: Use a local rain gauge or nearby verified weather record; for irrigation, record runtime and measured source/emitter output.
measure.frequency: For representative storms and irrigation events.

measure.method: Record when visible ponding begins and when each mapped low spot becomes free of standing water.
measure.frequency: After representative light, moderate and heavy events when possible.

measure.unit: sensor value or consistent qualitative class at recorded depth
measure.method: Check the same marked points and depths after water events. If no calibrated sensor is available, use a repeatable field class such as dry / moist / wet / saturated and label it qualitative.
measure.frequency: Before the event, shortly after, and again during drainage/dryback.

measure.method: Mark where water moves, deposits sediment or removes soil. Photograph from fixed references.
measure.frequency: After events that create visible runoff.

compare: high and low points on the same site
drainage time after different event intensities
root-zone response before and after bed, container, compaction or drainage changes
interpret: Rainfall depth is an input, not proof of root-zone recharge: interception, runoff and drainage change what roots experience.
Repeated long ponding at the same point indicates a different root-aeration risk than fast surface wetting followed by drainage.
A dry surface can coexist with deeper saturation, so depth must be recorded with the observation.
subtopics.decisionRule: Treat drainage as a time-and-depth pattern. Escalate site redesign or root-zone investigation when the same zones repeatedly remain saturated or erode while comparison zones recover normally.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: Do not convert qualitative hand-feel classes into volumetric water content unless the sensor/method has been calibrated for that medium.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Water access is a design constraint
subtopics.goal: Verify that the water source and delivery system can supply repeatable flow to the actual planting area before demand peaks.

measure.method: Collect water for a timed interval in a known-volume container and calculate volume ÷ time.
measure.frequency: Baseline before planting; repeat during high-demand periods or when performance changes.

measure.unit: L/min or gal/min at matched outlets
measure.method: Measure comparable outlets near the source and at the farthest/highest delivery point using the same test duration.
measure.frequency: At setup, after system changes and when uneven watering is suspected.

measure.method: Time how long the system requires to deliver a known volume or refill storage. Record simultaneous demand from other users/zones.

measure.unit: pH, EC and temperature when relevant
measure.method: Use calibrated meters and record units, calibration date and sampling point.
measure.frequency: Baseline and whenever source, season or water quality changes.

record: flow result and observed pressure problems
pH/EC units and meter calibration when measured
compare: source performance across dates and demand conditions
measured delivery against actual root-zone wetting rather than runtime alone
interpret: A source can provide adequate total water yet distribute it unevenly across distance, elevation or restricted emitters.
A stable runtime is not evidence of stable delivered volume if flow or pressure changes.
OSU field guidance shows hemp water response depends on production system and environment; site-specific delivery measurements are therefore more useful than copying one irrigation volume.
subtopics.decisionRule: Do not finalize the site or irrigation layout until the farthest intended point has been flow-tested and a repeatable way to verify root-zone wetting exists.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: Flow tests describe delivery capacity, not plant water requirement. Plant demand still depends on weather, root volume, genotype, spacing and medium.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Neighboring land can create biological and environmental risk
subtopics.goal: Turn surrounding pollen, dust, spray, water, vegetation and access risks into a mapped, time-stamped exposure record.

measure.method: Map known or observed neighboring sources from the crop boundary/planting area and record direction, not distance alone.
measure.frequency: Before planting and whenever neighboring land use changes.

measure.method: Use a local weather station or on-site wind observation and mark periods when wind arrives from the source sector toward the crop.
measure.frequency: During relevant flowering, spray, dust or smoke windows.

measure.method: Record when the neighboring source is active and when the crop is biologically or physically susceptible.
measure.frequency: Update as neighboring crop stage or activity becomes known.

measure.unit: location, severity class and photo ID
measure.method: Map where dust, drift-like injury, seed set or other suspected external effects appear before assigning a cause.
measure.frequency: After suspected exposure events and during routine scouting.

record: internal pollen/intersex findings when investigating seed set
compare: upwind vs downwind crop zones after a suspected event
dates with and without source-sector wind
internal and external explanations before assigning causality
interpret: Cannabis pollen risk is distance-dependent but meteorology creates a long dispersal tail; a single 'safe radius' is not scientifically defensible.
The 2024 U.S. pollen-dispersal study found strong spatial, seasonal and day/night variation, so direction and timing add information that distance alone cannot.
A mapped external source is a risk factor, not proof that it caused a specific symptom or seed set.
subtopics.decisionRule: Rate neighboring risk from source + direction + timing + observed pattern. Keep uncertainty explicit and avoid claiming zero risk from any universal isolation distance.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: Source identification and wind overlap improve attribution, but direct pollen or residue measurements would be needed for high-confidence exposure confirmation.

fieldWorksheet.title: Section 1 field record
fields: decision and what evidence would change it
fieldWorksheet.outcome: The learner should finish with a comparable site record, not merely a statement that the area is 'sunny', 'well drained' or 'has water'.
